summary.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q1 FY27: net profit up 27% YoY to INR2,020 crore, advances up 27%, NIM 3.85%, all guidance parameters beaten.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) with total business up 19% YoY, advances up 27% and deposits up 13%, against guidance of 16-17%, 18% and 14% respectively. Operating profit rose 21% YoY to INR3,117 crore and net profit rose 27% to INR2,020 crore. Asset quality held: gross NPA flat QoQ at 1.45%, net NPA 0.13%, credit cost 0.99%. Management kept its FY27 guidance unchanged despite the faster growth, and flagged the NIM (3.85%, down 10 bps YoY) and the rising cost of deposits QoQ as the points to watch.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY; retail gross NPA 0.34% per management, with home loan sanctions in the past 12 months 80% from CIBIL 750+ borrowers.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 30% YoY; agri gross NPA 7.58%, down from about 9% a couple of quarters back.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 23% YoY; MSME gross NPA 1.60%, and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 30% YoY, up from 17-18% in the prior four quarters; RAM:corporate mix at 63:37.

segments.name: IBU (GIFT City)
segments.commentary: IBU book about INR8,200 crore, contributing about 3 points of the 27% advances growth; sanctions of $965 million; global yield 8.57% vs domestic 8.66%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth guidance kept at 18%, despite Q1 growth of 27%; management said it would not revisit the number.
NIM guidance of 3.75% maintained; management said no further rate cuts are now expected and a rate hike may come.
Cost-to-income guided below 40%; Q1 running at about 36-38%.
Credit cost guided below 1%; Q1 at 0.99%.
Gross NPA guided below 2% and net NPA below 0.25%; Q1 at 1.45% and 0.13%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore planned this FY, with Board, shareholder and RBI approvals in place; awaiting government approval.
Tax rate guided at 12-13% on operating-profit basis and 16-17% on PBT basis.
Debt waiver scheme (under formulation): eligible portfolio about INR3,500 crore; expected to be settled within FY27; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions.
ECL: about INR125 crore per quarter of provisioning needed through March 2031, to be charged against net worth per RBI's final guidelines rather than P&L.
capex_capacity: Opening about 200 new branches a year under a 5-year expansion plan; new branches are staffed from day one.
Staff strength about INR17,500 crore (figure as stated) vs about INR13,000 crore two years ago; recruitment to continue.
Mobile banking app active registered users up from 2.75 lakh (old version) to over 14 lakh.
Around 40% of branches are in rural areas.
LCR average 118% vs terminal LCR 114%; management targets a 115-120% band.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 13% with no CDs raised in Q1; PSB average deposit growth 11% and private banks 14%, per management.
Domestic CD ratio 86%; 81.99% after including about INR19,000 crore of refinance (blended cost 6-6.5%).
Repo-linked share of loan book 53%, MCLR-linked 44%; MCLR was raised in the last two ALCO reviews and will reset gradually over the next year.
5-year FCNR deposit offered at 6.60%, positioned against the best PSB offers.
ECLGS: eligible portfolio INR6,700 crore, sanctions INR4,500 crore (65%), disbursed INR3,560 crore (82% of sanctions); MSME INR2,700 crore, corporate INR400 crore.
Retail term deposit growth 16% vs total deposits 13%; management attributes the QoQ rise in deposit cost to special retail TD schemes.
Gold loans about INR13,000 crore, up 75% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII (14.5%) lag advances growth (27%), and would management revisit the 18% loan growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept NII guidance of 15% and NIM of 3.75%, citing a branch-level profitability dashboard and tighter pricing. It said it would keep the 18% advances guidance, with IBU contributing 3 points of the 27% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current account balances fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it not a major concern: the decline is about 2,500-3,000 bps of the current account book, and CASA still grew 9% YoY, adding INR14,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Agri provisions and debt waiver impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligible portfolio INR3,500 crore; government receivable INR2,750 crore; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions. Settlement expected within FY27, plus INR50,000 per farmer incentive into SB accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate is about 12-13% on an operating-profit basis and 16-17% on a PBT basis, aided by rural advances (about 40% of branches rural), bad-debt write-off benefits and DTA.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost growth is driven by staffing new branches from day one; cost-to-income is 36-38% and guided below 40%. Branches opened three or more years ago have all turned profitable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury included a one-time SR of INR104 crore, with part of the payment possibly coming in later quarters; no treasury profit targets are set.

qa_highlights.question: SMA-2 jump from INR56 crore to INR208 crore; is MSME stress rising?
qa_highlights.answer: A single government entity account of INR87 crore moved into SMA-2 and is expected to regularise. SMA-1+2 stands at 1.34%, down 5 bps YoY.

risks_watch: Cost of deposits rose 5 bps QoQ to 4.38% and retail term deposits are growing faster than total deposits; watch the QoQ trend.
Thin CASA growth in Q1 (current account balances fell sharply QoQ) and reliance on refinance (about INR19,000 crore) and possible CDs as deposit growth lags loan growth.
Agri gross NPA at 7.58% and the debt-waiver haircut timing; the Rs 87 crore government account in SMA-2 needs to regularise.
Agri and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ (MSME 1.60%); watch for stress from geopolitical conditions (West Asia).
NIM pressure from MCLR resets, with the yield on advances down 71 bps YoY to 8.57% globally; the rate-hike benefit depends on repo-linked share at 53%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore pending government approval; treasury gains include a one-time item of INR104 crore.
ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on keeping guidance unchanged. Management was evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory, answering both with qualitative points rather than numbers.
key_quotes: We are committed to the guidance numbers that we have shared.
Gross NPA is maintained at the March level 1.45% against our guidance of maintaining it below 2%.
So refinance, again, why we decided not to go for high-cost bulk deposits, the blended cost that we have experienced while we go for refinance is in the range of 6% to 6.5%.
The mantra is very clear. It has to be a profitable growth and no compromise on the quality.

adds.what: About 200 new branches a year under a 5-year expansion plan (new branches staffed from day one)

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 18% (held despite Q1 advances +27% YoY), with total business guided 16-17%; backing is a branch expansion plan (~200 branches/yr) and a INR5,000 crore equity raise awaiting government approval, but no branch or capital numbers are tied to the 18% loan growth figure.
